questions.stem: These paired heart-and-circulation diagrams (normal, distributive, cardiogenic, hypovolemic, neurogenic, obstructive) are organized to convey what?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The hemodynamic mechanisms of the different categories of shock

choices.label: B
choices.text: The types of congestive heart failure

explanation.summary: Each panel contrasts blood flow and volume against a normal circulation to illustrate how the major categories of shock differ in their underlying hemodynamic derangement.
explanation.whyCorrect: Each panel contrasts blood flow and volume against a normal circulation to illustrate how the major categories of shock differ in their underlying hemodynamic derangement.

questions.stem: This hemodynamic graph shows cardiac output rising well above normal while both preload and afterload fall below normal. Which category of shock does this pattern represent?

explanation.summary: Widespread vasodilation lowers systemic vascular resistance (afterload) and venous return (preload), while a compensatory high cardiac output produces the warm, hyperdynamic profile typical of early distributive/septic shock.
explanation.whyCorrect: Widespread vasodilation lowers systemic vascular resistance (afterload) and venous return (preload), while a compensatory high cardiac output produces the warm, hyperdynamic profile typical of early distributive/septic shock.

questions.stem: This graph shows preload and afterload both increased while cardiac output is markedly decreased. Which category of shock does this represent?

explanation.summary: Pump failure lowers cardiac output while blood backs up (raising preload) and compensatory vasoconstriction raises afterload, the hallmark pattern of cardiogenic shock.
explanation.whyCorrect: Pump failure lowers cardiac output while blood backs up (raising preload) and compensatory vasoconstriction raises afterload, the hallmark pattern of cardiogenic shock.

questions.stem: This graph shows afterload increased while preload and cardiac output are both decreased. Which category of shock does this represent?

explanation.summary: Loss of intravascular volume drops venous return (preload) and cardiac output, while compensatory sympathetic vasoconstriction raises afterload, characteristic of hypovolemic shock.
explanation.whyCorrect: Loss of intravascular volume drops venous return (preload) and cardiac output, while compensatory sympathetic vasoconstriction raises afterload, characteristic of hypovolemic shock.

questions.stem: This graph shows preload, afterload, and cardiac output all decreased below normal. Which category of shock does this represent?

explanation.summary: Loss of sympathetic tone lowers vascular resistance (afterload) and venous return (preload) without a compensatory rise in output, so cardiac output also falls, the pattern of neurogenic shock.
explanation.whyCorrect: Loss of sympathetic tone lowers vascular resistance (afterload) and venous return (preload) without a compensatory rise in output, so cardiac output also falls, the pattern of neurogenic shock.

questions.stem: These paired graphs contrast right- and left-sided loading (e.g., raised RV preload but falling LV preload and cardiac output) depending on where flow is blocked. Which category of shock is depicted?

explanation.summary: A mechanical obstruction (e.g., pulmonary embolism or tamponade) impedes filling or ejection, so preload distributes unevenly across the ventricles while cardiac output falls, defining obstructive shock.
explanation.whyCorrect: A mechanical obstruction (e.g., pulmonary embolism or tamponade) impedes filling or ejection, so preload distributes unevenly across the ventricles while cardiac output falls, defining obstructive shock.
